definition_zh: 使窒息；噎住；阻塞；哽咽
definition_en: to be unable to breathe because something blocks the throat, to block a passage, or to lose the voice with strong feeling
core_image: 一只手按住喉咙，气卡在中间上不来
scene: 餐桌旁忽然静了，孩子捂着喉咙站起来。 He began to choke on a piece of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 choke 指「噎住」（第 1 个义项：有东西卡在喉咙而无法呼吸）；句意是他被一块面包噎住了。

derivatives.zh: 令人窒息的东西；贴颈项链
令人窒息的；噎住的
哽咽的；堵塞的

senses.title: To block the throat
senses.definition: to be unable to breathe because something blocks the throat
senses.definitionCN: 因有东西堵住喉咙而无法呼吸
senses.example: He began to choke on a fish bone.
senses.exampleCN: 他被一根鱼刺噎住了。
senses.why: The Old English word named the jaw and the throat, the very place where breath is stopped.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指颌与喉，正是呼吸被阻断的地方。

senses.title: To block a passage
senses.definition: to block or fill a passage so that things cannot move through
senses.definitionCN: 堵住通道，使东西无法通过
senses.example: Weeds choked the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 杂草堵塞了狭窄的水道。
senses.why: A blocked throat and a blocked channel share the same image of something jammed tight.
senses.whyCN: 喉咙被堵与通道被堵共享同一个死死卡住的意象。

senses.title: To lose the voice with feeling
senses.definition: to be unable to speak clearly because of strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 因情绪强烈而说不清话
senses.example: She choked back her tears and went on.
senses.exampleCN: 她强忍眼泪继续说了下去。
senses.why: Tears tighten the throat, so the word for the throat came to mean speech stopped by feeling.
senses.whyCN: 泪水使喉咙发紧，于是这个喉咙词也指被情绪堵住的话。

intro.en: Choke began as an Old English word for the jaw and the throat.
intro.cn: choke 原本是古英语中指颌与喉的词。

items.en: A root keuk- named the jaw and the swallowing throat.
items.cn: 词根 keuk- 指颌骨与吞咽的喉咙。

items.en: Aceocian meant to choke, beside ceoce for the jaw.
items.cn: aceocian 意为窒息，旁边还有 ceoce 指颌。

items.en: Choken narrowed to the stoppage of breath.
items.cn: choken 的词义收窄为呼吸受阻。

items.en: The same verb spread to blocked pipes and blocked roads.
items.cn: 同一个动词扩展到堵塞的管道与道路。

items.en: The throat image produced the sense of speech stopped by emotion.
items.cn: 喉咙的意象又生出被情绪堵住话的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch sound, while the meaning group names ways of stopping breath.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch 音，近义组列出各种使呼吸停滞的说法。

entries.definition: the soft side of the face below the eye
entries.definitionCN: 眼睛下方柔软的面部侧面

entries.definition: a group of people who sing together
a building used for Christian worship
entries.definitionCN: 用于基督教礼拜的建筑

entries.definition: to die or suffer from lack of air
to kill by pressing hard on the throat
to choke and nearly vomit

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw origin, the throat image and the three everyday phrase families.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌骨来源、喉咙意象以及三组日常搭配。

normal.en: Choke and cheek are cousins: the throat that chokes sits right beside the cheek.
normal.cn: choke 与 cheek 是亲戚：噎住的喉咙就在脸颊旁边。

normal.en: Choke on food, choke back tears, choke off supplies: the particle shows what is blocked.
normal.cn: choke on food、choke back tears、choke off supplies，小品词标出被堵住的东西。

normal.en: A choked voice is a throat tightened by feeling, not by food.
normal.cn: a choked voice 是被情绪而非食物勒紧的喉咙。

normal.en: A drain choked with leaves repeats the blocked channel sense exactly.
normal.cn: a drain choked with leaves 完全重复了通道堵塞那一义。

normal.en: The noun choke names the sound and the valve that cuts off air.
normal.cn: 名词 choke 指那种声音，也指截断空气的阀门。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rising to a throat in the middle of a meal.
abstract.cn: 想象吃饭吃到一半，一只手猛地捂上喉咙。

abstract.en: Picture weeds packed so tight that water cannot pass.
abstract.cn: 想象杂草挤得密不透风，水一点也过不去。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker stopping mid sentence with shining eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象说话的人眼睛发亮，话说到一半停住。

examples.en: The thick smoke made him choke.
examples.cn: 浓烟呛得他喘不上气。

examples.en: Anger choked his words for a moment.
examples.cn: 愤怒让他一时说不出话。

examples.en: The drain was choked with wet leaves.
examples.cn: 排水口被湿叶子堵住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: choke 与 cheek 同源：卡住的正是紧挨脸颊的那段喉咙。

root: 源自古英语 aceocian（窒息），与 ceoce（颌、颊）同源，本指喉咙被堵住而无法呼吸。

sensesIntro.en: A blocked throat gives the bodily sense, which spreads to blocked passages and then to speech stopped by feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 喉咙被堵给出身体义，随后扩展到堵塞的通道，再扩展到被情绪堵住的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath stuck halfway down a narrowed throat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气卡在收窄的喉咙中间。

branches.en: Food in the throat stops the breath at once.
branches.cn: 食物卡在喉里，呼吸立刻停住。

branches.en: Pipes and roads repeat the same jam on a larger scale.
branches.cn: 管道与道路把同一种堵塞放大到更大范围。

branches.en: Tears press on the throat until words fail.
branches.cn: 泪水压住喉咙，直到话语出不来。

branches.en: Body and feeling both tighten the same passage.
branches.cn: 身体与情绪收紧的是同一条通道。

branches.en: Throat and channel share one verb of blocking.
branches.cn: 喉咙与通道共用一个表示堵塞的动词。

intro.en: The short stem choke carries the verb, its inflections and two compound nouns.
intro.cn: 短词干 choke 支撑动词、各种屈折形式以及两个复合名词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin: Old English ceoce for the jaw lies behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，背后是古英语 ceoce（颌）。

items.example: He chokes whenever he eats too fast.
items.exampleCN: 他每次吃得太快都会噎住。

items.example: The dust was choking the workers.
items.exampleCN: 灰尘呛得工人喘不过气。

items.meaning: a thing that chokes or a tight necklace
items.meaningCN: 令人窒息之物或贴颈项链
items.exampleCN: 她戴着一条黑色贴颈项链。

items.meaning: a thing or person that acts

latinEntries.example: Ceoce is the old jaw word behind choke.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ceoce 是 choke 背后的古颌骨词。

definition_zh: 承认；坦白；供认；忏悔
definition_en: to admit that you have done something wrong
core_image: 一个人低着头，把藏在心里很久的事说出来
scene: 审讯室里，他终于承认自己拿了那笔钱。 He finally confessed that he had taken the money.
sceneCN: 这里 confess 指「承认」（第 1 个义项：说出自己做过的错事）；句意是他终于承认自己拿了那笔钱。

derivatives.zh: 坦白；供词；忏悔
听忏悔的神父
自认的；公开承认的
忏悔的；坦白的

senses.title: Admit a personal fault
senses.definition: to admit to other people that you did something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向别人承认自己做了错事
senses.example: She confessed that she had lost the key.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认自己把钥匙弄丢了。
senses.why: A fault kept inside grows, and saying it out loud lets it shrink.
senses.whyCN: 藏着的过错会变大，说出口反而让它缩小。

senses.title: Admit a crime to police
senses.definition: to tell the police or a court that you committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 向警方或法庭说明自己犯了罪
senses.example: The man confessed to the robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 那名男子供认了抢劫行为。
senses.why: The law needs a clear statement before a case can be closed.
senses.whyCN: 案件要了结，法律需要一份清楚的陈述。

senses.title: Tell one's sins in church
senses.definition: to tell a priest about your sins and ask for forgiveness
senses.definitionCN: 向神父说出自己的罪并请求宽恕
senses.example: He went to church to confess his sins.
senses.exampleCN: 他去教堂忏悔自己的罪。
senses.why: The oldest sense is religious: a burden is handed over to a higher power.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义与宗教有关：把重担交给更高的力量。

intro.en: Confess comes from Latin confiteri, to admit fully, built from com-, completely, and fateri, to acknowledge.
intro.cn: confess 来自拉丁语 confiteri，意为彻底承认，由 com-（完全）与 fateri（承认）构成。

items.en: Fateri meant to admit or declare something openly.
items.cn: fateri 意为公开承认或声明某事。

items.en: Confiteri strengthened the act into a full and open admission.
items.cn: confiteri 把这一行为加强为彻底而公开的承认。

items.en: Old French confesser used the word mainly for religious confession.
items.cn: 古法语 confesser 主要把这个词用于宗教告解。

items.en: English confess first meant to declare one's sins to a priest.
items.cn: 英语 confess 最初指向神父告明自己的罪。

items.en: It now also covers admitting a fault or a crime in everyday life.
items.cn: 如今它也覆盖日常生活中承认错误或罪行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that share the ending of confess, and the meaning group names other ways of admitting something.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confess 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他表示承认的说法。

entries.definition: to state a belief or feeling openly
to make someone unable to think clearly
to face a problem or person directly
to agree that something is true
to accept that a fact is real
to make something hidden known

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a secret held too long, then move to a police room and to a quiet church.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从藏得太久的秘密开始，再走到警局房间与安静的教堂。

normal.en: Con- is fully and fess- is admit, so to confess is to admit fully.
normal.cn: con- 是完全，fess- 是承认，所以 confess 就是彻底承认。

normal.en: A confession is a door that only opens from the inside.
normal.cn: 坦白是一扇只能从里面打开的门。

normal.en: Confess and confession share the same body, one is the act and one is the words.
normal.cn: confess 与 confession 同根，一个是动作，一个是说出口的话。

normal.en: In church, confession is spoken in a whisper; in court, in a clear voice.
normal.cn: 在教堂里，忏悔是低声说的；在法庭上，供认是清楚说的。

normal.en: The moment you confess, the secret stops being heavy.
normal.cn: 你说出真相的那一刻，秘密就不再沉重。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening a clenched fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手慢慢松开紧握的拳头。

abstract.en: Picture a small dark room with one narrow window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间只有一扇窄窗的小黑屋。

abstract.en: Picture a stone lifted off a covered well.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头从井口上被搬开。

examples.en: He confessed that he had broken the window.
examples.cn: 他承认自己打破了窗户。

examples.en: She refused to confess to a crime she did not commit.
examples.cn: 她拒绝供认自己没有犯过的罪。

examples.en: The old man went to confess before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节日前那位老人去做了忏悔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confess 记成 con（完全）加 fess（说）：把藏在心里的事完全说出来，就是承认与忏悔。

root: 源自拉丁语 confiteri（com 完全 + fateri 承认），本义是完全承认，后引申为坦白、供认与宗教忏悔。

sensesIntro.en: From a personal fault spoken aloud, to a crime admitted to police, and finally to sins told in church.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出口的个人过失，到向警方供认的罪行，最后到在教堂告明的罪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that has held a secret for years finally opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只握了许多年秘密的手终于松开。

branches.en: Everyday confession is about a small fault and a relieved mind.
branches.cn: 日常的承认关乎一个小过失与一颗放松下来的心。

branches.en: Legal confession turns private knowledge into public record.
branches.cn: 法律上的供认把私下的知情变成公开记录。

branches.en: Religious confession hands the weight to a higher power.
branches.cn: 宗教忏悔把重担交给更高的力量。

branches.en: Both ask for forgiveness, one from a person and one from heaven.
branches.cn: 两者都请求宽恕，一个向人，一个向上天。

branches.en: A court confession is only the everyday act with the law listening.
branches.cn: 法庭上的供认，不过是日常承认多了法律在听。

intro.en: Confess is built on Latin com-, fully, plus fateri, to admit.
intro.cn: confess 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 fateri（承认）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin admit base fess- also appears in profession and profess.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的承认词基 fess- 也出现在 profession 与 profess 中。

items.example: He sat confessing to the officer.
The letter had a confessional tone.
items.exampleCN: 这封信带着忏悔的语气。

items.example: They profess great interest in the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们声称对这个计划很有兴趣。

definition_zh: 向上的；上升的；朝上地；向高处；以上
definition_en: moving or pointing towards a higher place or level
core_image: 一支箭斜斜地指向天空
scene: 报告的总页数超过一千，编辑把折线图往上一拉，曲线明显在爬升。 The sales curve has been steadily upward all year.
sceneCN: 这里 upward 是「向上的」（第 1 个义项：方向或趋势朝上）；句意为销售曲线一整年都在稳步往上。斜指天空的箭头，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 upward 加 -s 构成的副词变体，义为「向上；以上」
由 upward 加 -ly 构成，义为「向上地」，多见于 upwardly mobile
把 up 换成 down 构成的反义形式，义为「向下的」

senses.title: Moving or pointing to a higher place
senses.definition: directed towards a higher position
senses.definitionCN: 朝更高的位置去
senses.example: He gave an upward glance at the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他往上瞥了一眼窗户。
senses.why: The word is up with the suffix -ward, which marks direction, so it names the way up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 加上表示方向的词尾 -ward，指的就是「朝上的方向」。

senses.title: Rising in amount or level
senses.definition: used of figures or trends that are rising
senses.definitionCN: 形容数值或趋势在升高
senses.example: There is upward pressure on wages.
senses.exampleCN: 工资面临上行压力。
senses.why: Direction in space turns into direction on a chart, and a rising line is simply an upward one.
senses.whyCN: 空间里的方向转成图表上的方向，往上的线就是 upward。

senses.title: More than a stated number
senses.definition: used in the phrase upward of with a figure
senses.definitionCN: 用于 upward of 加数字的说法
senses.example: Upward of two hundred people came.
senses.exampleCN: 来了两百多人。
senses.why: A figure read on the rising side of a mark means at least that much, so upward of sets a lower limit.
senses.whyCN: 在刻度上升的一侧读数字，就表示「至少这么多」，所以 upward of 划出的是一条下限。

senses.title: Towards a better position or class
senses.definition: used with mobility for movement to a higher social class
senses.definitionCN: 与 mobility 连用，指社会阶层的上升
senses.example: Education is still the main route to upward mobility.
senses.exampleCN: 教育仍是向上流动的主要途径。
senses.why: The ladder picture carries over: the higher rungs stand for rank, so climbing upward means rising in class.
senses.whyCN: 梯子的图景继续延伸：台阶越高代表等级越高，往上爬就是阶层上升。

senses.title: Facing or lying with the top turned up
senses.definition: used of a surface or a face turned towards the sky
senses.definitionCN: 形容表面或面孔朝着天空
senses.example: He lay face upward on the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 他仰面躺在草地上。
senses.why: The direction of the arrow also works for a face: its front is turned towards the sky, which is upward.
senses.whyCN: 箭头的方向同样适用于脸：正面对着天空，也就是朝上。

intro.en: An old adverb with the very common suffix that turns words into directions.
intro.cn: 一个古老的副词加上极常见的、把词变成方向的词尾。

items.en: Up is an old adverb, and the suffix -weard meant turning towards.
items.cn: up 是古副词，词尾 -weard 意为「转向……」。

items.en: The form upweard names the direction towards the top.
items.cn: upweard 这一形式指朝上的方向。

items.en: Upward and upwards both circulate, the second commoner when speaking of quantities.
items.cn: upward 与 upwards 同时流行，后者在谈数量时更常见。

items.en: The adjective use settles in phrases like upward trend and upward pressure.
items.cn: 形容词用法固定于 upward trend、upward pressure 这类短语。

items.en: Upward of becomes the standard way to say more than a figure.
items.cn: upward of 成为表示「超过某数」的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the -ward family, while the near-meaning group collects words for rising and for direction.
note.cn: 形近组沿 -ward 词族展开，近义组汇集表示上升与方向的说法。

entries.definition: towards the top
upward
towards the bottom
towards the front
towards the back
going up
going up
moving steadily higher
at right angles to the ground

normalIntro.en: A direction word made by the commonest of suffixes, useful in charts and reports.
normalIntro.cn: 由最常见的词尾构成的方向词，在图表与报告里很实用。

normal.en: Up plus -ward, the suffix of direction, as in forward and backward.
normal.cn: up 加 -ward，方向词尾，如 forward、backward。

normal.en: Upward trend and upward pressure are the two collocations to master.
normal.cn: upward trend 与 upward pressure 是最该掌握的搭配。

normal.en: Upward of means more than, never less than.
normal.cn: upward of 意为「超过」，绝不是「少于」。

normal.en: Adjective before a noun, adverb after a verb: the position tells you the job.
normal.cn: 放名词前是形容词，放动词后是副词：位置说明词性。

normal.en: Upwards with an s is the usual spoken adverb form.
normal.cn: 带 s 的 upwards 是口语中常见的副词形式。

abstract.en: See an arrow leaning towards the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一支斜指天空的箭。

abstract.en: Watch a line on a graph keep climbing.
abstract.cn: 看图上一条线一路往上爬。

abstract.en: Feel a hand turn a palm towards the ceiling.
abstract.cn: 体会一只把手掌翻向天花板。

examples.en: The chart shows a slow upward movement in wages.
examples.cn: 图表显示工资在缓慢上行。

examples.en: He nodded upward towards the noise on the roof.
examples.cn: 他朝屋顶上传来声响的方向点了点头。

examples.en: Upward of forty people signed the list.
examples.cn: 四十多人在这份名单上签了字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普沃德」——阿普沃德家的烟囱里，烟一个劲儿地往上冒。

root: 古英语 upweard，由 up（向上）与方向词尾 -weard（朝……转）构成，现代英语中固定为 upward，并有副词变体 upwards

sensesIntro.en: One direction towards the top supplies space, charts, figures, social class, and a face turned to the sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个朝上的方向，覆盖空间、图表、数字、社会阶层与仰起的脸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow tilted towards the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：斜指天空的箭。

branches.en: The space branch: eyes, hands, or arrows turn up.
branches.cn: 空间分支：目光、手或箭头朝上。

branches.en: The figure branch: a trend that climbs on paper.
branches.cn: 数据分支：纸面上一路上行的趋势。

branches.en: The quantity branch: upward of a stated number.
branches.cn: 数量分支：超过某个给定的数目。

branches.en: The class branch: moving to a better position.
branches.cn: 阶层分支：向更好的位置移动。

branches.en: The surface branch: a palm turned to the ceiling.
branches.cn: 表面分支：掌心翻向天花板。

intro.en: A very productive direction suffix over the oldest of adverbs.
intro.cn: 一个极能产的方向词尾压在最为古老的副词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin handles the same idea with sursum for the adverb and adjectives like superus for higher.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 sursum 表副词方向，用 superus 一类形容词表「上方的」。

definition_zh: 树皮；狗叫；厉声说
definition_en: the outer cover of a tree, or the short loud sound a dog makes
core_image: 老树干上裂开的粗糙树皮
scene: 院子里的狗突然竖起耳朵。 A dog barked at the gate.

derivatives.zh: 由 bark 加 -ing 构成，义为「吠叫声」

senses.title: A piece of old cloth
senses.definition: a torn or worn piece of cloth, often used for cleaning
senses.definitionCN: 一块破烂或旧损的布，常用来擦拭
senses.example: He wiped the floor with a rag.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一块破布擦地板。
senses.why: The word is probably from an old northern term for a tattered scrap, and the cleaning cloth is simply the everyday use of such a scrap.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能来自古老的北方方言，指破烂的碎片，而擦洗用的布正是这种碎片的日常用途。

senses.title: Torn or dirty clothes
senses.definition: old and torn clothing, almost always in the plural

senses.example: The child was dressed in rags.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子穿着破烂衣服。
senses.why: A worn cloth and a worn garment are the same kind of thing, so the plural came to mean a whole set of tattered clothes.
senses.whyCN: 破布与破衣本是同一类东西，于是复数形式转指一整套褴褛的衣物。

senses.title: A low-quality newspaper
senses.definition: a newspaper, especially one that is poorly produced or sensational
senses.definitionCN: 报纸，尤指制作粗糙或专事耸动的报纸
senses.example: The story appeared in a local rag.
senses.exampleCN: 这则消息登在一家本地小报上。
senses.why: A paper that is thrown away like a cloth is insulted by being called a rag, a common English habit of naming things by their cheapness.

senses.title: To tease someone

senses.example: The older boys ragged him about his accent.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的男孩们拿他的口音取笑他。
senses.why: Teasing that pulls a person about is pictured as handling them like a scrap of cloth, which gives the verb its rough playfulness.
senses.whyCN: 把人来回拉扯的取笑，被想象成把对方当作一块破布那样摆弄，这赋予动词一种粗野的玩笑意味。

intro.en: Rag is a word of uncertain origin, probably northern English or Scandinavian, first naming a tattered scrap of cloth; no reliable Latin source can be given.
intro.cn: rag 来源不确定，很可能是英格兰北部或斯堪的纳维亚来源，最初指破烂的布片；无法给出可靠的拉丁语来源。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English, and dictionaries trace it to northern dialect rather than to Latin or French.
items.cn: 这个词见于中古英语，词典把它追溯到北方方言，而不是拉丁语或法语。

items.en: The earliest sense was a torn piece of cloth, the kind used for wiping and cleaning.
items.cn: 最早的意思是撕破的布片，正是用来擦拭清洁的那一类。

items.en: By the later Middle Ages the plural rags meant torn clothing worn by poor people.
items.cn: 到中古晚期，复数 rags 指穷人穿的破衣。

items.en: Later English applied the word to cheap newspapers and to rough teasing, both suggesting something of little value.
items.cn: 后来的英语把这个词用到廉价报纸与粗野的取笑上，两者都暗示「不值钱」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the cloth, the clothes, the newspaper and the verb of playful mocking.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了破布、破衣、报纸，以及戏弄这个动词。

note.cn: 形近组收由同一短词根构成的形式；近义组收表示布片与廉价报纸的词。

senses.title: To keep apart from others
senses.definition: to separate a person, place, or group from others, often for safety or health
senses.definitionCN: 把某人、某地或某群体与他人分开，常出于安全或健康原因
senses.example: The clinic isolated new arrivals for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把新到的人隔离了两周。
senses.why: The verb was built on Latin insula, an island, so isolating is making an island of someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在拉丁语 insula「岛」上，隔离就是把人围成一座岛。

senses.title: To feel cut off
senses.definition: to make someone feel alone and unable to take part in what others do
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在情感上孤独，无法参与他人的活动
senses.example: The language barrier isolated him at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 语言障碍让他在聚会上很孤立。
senses.why: Social isolation repeats the same ring of water, now made of language and custom.
senses.whyCN: 社会层面的孤立还是那一圈水，只是换成了语言和习惯。

senses.title: To separate a part
senses.definition: to take one part or element away from the rest so it can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 把其中一部分或一个要素从整体中取出来单独研究
senses.example: Engineers isolated the faulty wire from the system.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把故障电线从系统里单独分离出来。
senses.why: Separating one element is like lifting one island out of a larger land mass.
senses.whyCN: 把一个要素单拿出来，就像从一整块陆地里抬出一座岛。

senses.title: To obtain a pure substance
senses.definition: to obtain a substance in a pure form, free of everything mixed with it
senses.definitionCN: 得到纯净的物质，去掉其中混杂的其它成分
senses.example: Chemists isolated the active compound from the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家从叶子中分离出了活性化合物。
senses.why: The chemistry sense is the physical version of taking one thing out of a mixture.
senses.whyCN: 化学义是「从混合物中取出一样东西」的物理版本。

senses.title: Standing alone in grammar
senses.definition: describing a language or word form that has no clear relatives or partners
senses.definitionCN: 描述没有明确亲属关系或搭配形式的语言或词形
senses.example: The dialect is an isolated form with no close relatives.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言是一种没有近亲的孤立形式。
senses.why: In linguistics the island image turns into a form with no bridges to anything else.
senses.whyCN: 在语言学里，岛的意象变成了没有任何桥梁可通的形式。

intro.en: Isolate was formed in English in the early nineteenth century from the Latin adjective insulatus, "made into an island".
intro.cn: isolate 是十九世纪初英语造出的词，源自拉丁语形容词 insulatus「被围成岛的」。

items.en: insula meant island and also named a block of flats.
items.cn: insula 意为岛，也指一栋公寓楼。

items.en: insulatus meant made into an island, set apart.
items.cn: insulatus 意为被围成岛的、被隔开的。

items.en: Italian isolato, isolated, gave the verb its -ate shape.
items.cn: 意大利语 isolato「被隔离的」给了这个词 -ate 的形状。

items.en: French isoler appears in the eighteenth century with the same meaning.
items.cn: 法语 isoler 在十八世纪出现，意义相同。

items.en: English formed the verb isolate, and the chemistry sense came in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语造出动词 isolate，化学义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the insul- or isol- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for separating and excluding.
note.cn: 形近组共用 insul-、isol- 词干；近义组收表示分开与排斥的词。

entries.definition: The state of being separated from others.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「隔离状态」，同族名词。

entries.definition: To protect something with a barrier.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「隔热、绝缘」，词干同为 insul-。

entries.definition: Cut off from others.

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: keeping people apart, social loneliness, separating a part, obtaining a pure substance, and an isolated language form.

definition_zh: 膝部；一圈；一段路程；舔食；轻拍
definition_en: the flat area of the legs when sitting, one circuit of a track, a stage of a journey, or the act of drinking with the tongue
core_image: 老人坐在藤椅上，膝头摊开一本旧相册
scene: 傍晚，老人坐在门廊的藤椅上，翻着一本旧相册。 The child fell asleep on her mother's lap before the story ended.
sceneCN: 这里是「膝部」（第 1 个义项：人坐着时大腿到膝盖的区域）；句意为故事还没讲完，孩子就在母亲的膝上睡着了。可辨识画面：门廊、藤椅、旧相册。

derivatives.zh: 由 lap 与 top 复合，本指放在膝上使用的电脑，义为「笔记本电脑」

senses.title: The flat area of the legs when sitting
senses.definition: the flat space formed by your thighs when you are sitting down
senses.definitionCN: 坐着时由大腿形成的平坦区域
senses.example: She held the baby on her lap.
senses.exampleCN: 她把婴儿抱在膝上。
senses.why: The word first named a fold of cloth hanging over the legs, and from that covered area it came to mean the legs themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指垂在腿前的衣摆，从被衣摆盖住的这片区域转指腿本身。

senses.title: One circuit of a racing track
senses.definition: one complete circuit of a track, as in a race
senses.definitionCN: 跑道上完整的一圈，如比赛中的一圈
senses.example: He set the fastest lap of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他跑出了这场比赛的最快一圈。
senses.why: A lap was once a fold or a length of something, and the sense of one length around a course grew from covering the same ground again.
senses.whyCN: lap 曾指一段折叠或长度，绕行全程一遍的意味就从「又走完一段同样的路」长出来。

senses.title: One stage of a journey
senses.definition: one stage of a longer journey or race
senses.definitionCN: 较长旅程或比赛中的一个阶段
senses.example: The last lap of the tour took them north.
senses.exampleCN: 旅程的最后一段把他们带向北方。
senses.why: If a lap is one measured stretch, a journey becomes a series of such stretches, so the word names each of them.
senses.whyCN: 既然一圈是量好的一段，旅程就成了若干段这样的叠加，这个词便逐段指称。

senses.title: To drink with the tongue
senses.definition: to drink by moving the tongue, as animals do
senses.definitionCN: 像动物那样用舌头舔着喝
senses.example: The cat lapped the milk from the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 猫舔着碗里的牛奶。
senses.why: Old English had a separate verb lapian for licking up liquid, and it simply merged in spelling with the noun.
senses.whyCN: 古英语另有一个动词 lapian 表示舔饮液体，它只是在拼写上与名词合并了。

senses.title: To wash against a surface softly
senses.definition: to move against a surface with a soft, repeated sound
senses.definitionCN: 带着轻柔的重复声响拍打表面
senses.example: Small waves lapped the side of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 细浪轻拍着船舷。
senses.why: Water touching a surface again and again imitates the licking motion, so the licking verb stretched to waves.
senses.whyCN: 水一遍遍触碰表面，像重复舔舐，于是「舔」的动词被拉去形容波浪。

intro.en: Two Old English nouns and one Old English verb lie behind this word, and racing later gave it the sense of a circuit.
intro.cn: 两个古英语名词与一个古英语动词构成了这个词，赛马后来又给了它「一圈」的意思。

items.en: Læppa meant a fold or flap of cloth, the piece that hangs down over the body.
items.cn: læppa 意为布料的褶、垂下的衣摆。

items.en: A separate verb lapian meant to lick up liquid with the tongue.
items.cn: 另有一个动词 lapian，意为用舌头舔饮液体。

items.en: Middle English lap moved from the cloth over the legs to the legs themselves.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lap 从盖在腿上的衣摆转指腿本身。

items.en: Racing and travel added the sense of one measured stretch of a course.
items.cn: 赛马与旅行加上了「赛道上一段、一圈」的意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for legs, circuits and stages, and the verb for licking and for waves.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词的腿、圈与路段义，也保留动词的舔食与拍打义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words that differ by one letter; the near-meaning group collects words for knees, circuits and licking.
note.cn: 形近组收只差一个字母的短词；近义组收表示膝盖、圈与舔的词。

normal.en: Lap up means to take in eagerly, like a cat licking up milk.

abstract.en: One spelling holds a fold, a circuit and a lick, three histories that met only in English.

abstract.en: A lap is a unit of return: you go all the way round and come back to where you began.
abstract.cn: 一圈是回归的单位：绕行全程，再回到起点。

definition_zh: 当…的时候；虽然；然而（英式书面，同 while）
definition_en: a British and rather formal form of while, used to say that two things happen at the same time or that two facts differ
core_image: 同一个钟面上多加了一个小小的 t 形刻度
scene: 一封英式公函里写道：请在此等候，同时我们核对手续。 Please wait whilst we check your documents.
sceneCN: 这里 whilst 是「当…的时候」（第 1 个义项：与 while 同义的英式书面形式）；句意为请在此稍候，我们核对一下您的证件。同一个钟面上多出一个 t 形小刻度的画面就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 当…的时候（常用形式）
在…之中（同类 -st 形式）

senses.title: During the time that
senses.definition: used in formal British writing to say that one thing happens during the time of another
senses.definitionCN: 在正式英式写作中表示一件事发生在另一件事进行的那段时间里
senses.example: Please wait whilst we check your documents.
senses.exampleCN: 请在此稍候，我们核对一下您的证件。
senses.why: Whilest arose as an adverbial form of while, and the extra ending never changed the during meaning.
senses.whyCN: whilest 本是 while 的副词形式，多出的词尾从未改变「当…时」的意思。

senses.title: Although
senses.definition: used in formal writing to admit a fact that makes the main clause surprising
senses.definitionCN: 在正式写作中承认一个使主句显得意外的事实
senses.example: Whilst the results are encouraging, more tests are needed.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管结果令人鼓舞，还需要更多测试。
senses.why: Because the word is only a formal twin of while, it inherits every sense of its partner.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是 while 的正式孪生形式，所以继承了搭档的全部义项。

senses.title: Whereas
senses.definition: used in formal prose to set two facts against each other
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文章中把两个事实并排对照
senses.example: Some departments grew, whilst others were cut.
senses.exampleCN: 有些部门扩大了，而另一些被裁减。
senses.why: A formal register suits official documents, where contrasts are stated plainly and without emotion.
senses.whyCN: 正式语体适合公文，那里对比总是平铺直叙、不带情绪。

senses.title: A marker of style
senses.definition: used to give a formal or slightly old-fashioned tone to a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 为文章添上正式或略带古旧的语气
senses.example: The notice reads: no entry whilst the lights are on.
senses.exampleCN: 告示上写着：灯亮时禁止入内。
senses.why: The t survives mainly because of print and legal habits, not because it says anything extra.
senses.whyCN: 这个 t 主要靠印刷与法律习惯保留下来，并不因为它多表达了什么。

intro.en: Whilst is while with the old adverbial ending -st, the same one that produced amongst and against.
intro.cn: whilst 是 while 加上古老的副词词尾 -st，与 amongst、against 的一模一样。

items.en: The noun hwīl meant a period of time; there was no form ending in -st yet.
items.cn: 名词 hwīl 意为一段时间，当时还没有以 -st 结尾的形式。

items.en: A new shortening whilest appeared beside while, built with the old ending -es or -st.
items.cn: 与 while 并列出现了一个缩短的形式 whilest，由古老的词尾 -es 或 -st 构成。

items.en: Printers settled the spelling whilst, and it spread in British official prose.
items.cn: 印刷商把拼写定为 whilst，它在英式公文中传播开来。

items.en: American usage dropped whilst almost entirely and kept while.
items.cn: 美式用法几乎完全舍弃了 whilst，只保留 while。

items.en: British writers keep it as a marker of formal or slightly elderly style.
items.cn: 英国作者保留它，作为正式或略带回旧语体的标志。

note.en: The first group collects the other -st forms that look alike, the second the plain words whilst can always be replaced by.
note.cn: 第一组收其他形近的 -st 形式，第二组收随时可以替换 whilst 的朴素说法。

normal.en: If in doubt, write while; whilst belongs to letters and notices.

definition_zh: 紧张地；不安地；局促地；焦躁地
definition_en: in an anxious or worried way; with shy awkwardness; in a restless, fidgety manner
core_image: 长椅上的一支笔在指间转个不停，桌角的纸被折了又展平
scene: 面试室外的长椅上，年轻人低头坐着，一支笔在指间转个不停。 He tapped his foot nervously while waiting for his name to be called.
sceneCN: 这里是「紧张不安地」（第 1 个义项：心里发紧、动作无法放松）；句意为等叫名字的时候，他紧张地一直跺脚。图中可辨识物件：长椅、转动的笔、折过的纸角。

pos.zh: 紧张地；不安地；局促地；焦躁地

derivatives.zh: nervously 的词根，义为「紧张的；神经的」
由 nervous 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧张；神经质」
nervous 的来源词，义为「神经；勇气」

senses.title: In an anxious, worried manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows worry and an inability to relax
senses.definitionCN: 以显出担忧、无法放松的方式
senses.example: He tapped his foot nervously while waiting for his name to be called.
senses.exampleCN: 等叫名字的时候，他紧张地一直跺脚。
senses.why: The ending -ly turns the adjective of taut nerves into the manner of an action, so nervously always describes a body that cannot settle while it waits.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示「神经绷紧」的形容词变成动作的方式，所以 nervously 描述的总是等待时无法安顿下来的身体。

senses.title: With shy awkwardness
senses.definition: in a shy, awkward way that shows a person is unsure what to do or say
senses.definitionCN: 以害羞、笨拙的方式，显出不确定该做什么或说什么
senses.example: She laughed nervously and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她局促地笑了笑，把话题岔开。
senses.why: Social pressure produces the same tightness as danger does, and the small, mismatched movements it causes are read by others as awkwardness, so the adverb also names the manner of someone out of place.
senses.whyCN: 社交压力造成的紧绷与危险带来的紧绷相同，由此产生的小而失当的动作在旁人眼里就是局促，所以这个副词也命名「格格不入」时的举止。

senses.title: In a restless, fidgety manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows repeated small movements caused by tension
senses.definitionCN: 以因紧张而反复做出小动作的方式
senses.example: The boy shifted nervously in his chair all through the film.
senses.exampleCN: 整场电影里，那个男孩都在椅子上焦躁地挪来挪去。
senses.why: Restlessness is tension expressed through repetition, and the adverb reports the rhythm of those tiny movements rather than the feeling behind them.
senses.whyCN: 坐立不安是把紧张通过重复动作表达出来，这个副词报告的是那些细微动作的节奏，而不是背后的感受。

intro.en: Nervously is the adjective of taut nerves fitted with the English manner ending, so its history is the history of nervous plus -ly.
intro.cn: nervously 是表示「神经绷紧」的形容词配上英语方式词尾，它的历史就是 nervous 加 -ly 的历史。

items.en: Nervus meant sinew or tendon, the cord that keeps a body taut and ready.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋或肌腱，是让身体绷紧、随时待命的索。

items.en: Nervosus meant full of sinew and therefore strong, and it gave English the adjective nervous.
items.cn: nervosus 意为多筋的、因而强壮的，它给英语提供了形容词 nervous。

items.en: English nervous moved from praising strength to naming quick reactions and then everyday worry.
items.cn: 英语的 nervous 从称赞力量，转到指反应迅捷，再转到日常的担忧。

items.en: The Old English ending -lice became -ly, turning adjectives of state into adverbs of how an action is carried out.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 变成 -ly，把表示状态的形容词变成说明动作如何进行的方式副词。

items.en: Modern English uses nervously for waiting, laughing, glancing and shifting, keeping one adverb for every visible form of tension.
items.cn: 现代英语把 nervously 用于等待、发笑、瞥视与挪动，各种看得见的紧张都用同一个副词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the abstract noun and the root noun of the same family; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs of fear and strain.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形容词、抽象名词与词根名词；近义组收其他表示恐惧与紧绷的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective of anxiety and of the nerves themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 表示焦虑以及神经本身的形容词。

entries.definition: The state that nervously describes when it appears in an action.
entries.definitionCN: nervously 所描述的那种状态本身。

entries.definition: The fibre, or the courage and boldness that share its name.
entries.definitionCN: 纤维，或与之同名的勇气与放肆。

entries.definition: Anxious in British English, bold in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语指紧张，美式英语指有胆量。

entries.definition: In a worried way, often with a sense of waiting for bad news.
entries.definitionCN: 以担忧的方式，常带等待坏消息的意味。

entries.definition: With the body or atmosphere drawn tight, stressing strain rather than fear.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或气氛绷得很紧，强调吃力而非害怕。

entries.definition: In a mildly worried or uncomfortable way, softer than nervously.
entries.definitionCN: 以略有担忧或不适的方式，语气比 nervously 轻。

entries.definition: In a shy, fearful way, stressing lack of confidence rather than tension.
entries.definitionCN: 以羞怯、害怕的方式，强调缺乏自信而非紧绷。

normalIntro.en: The word is nervous with the manner ending -ly, so it reports how tension shows itself in small actions.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 nervous 加方式词尾 -ly，所以它报告的是紧张如何通过细小动作显出来。

normal.en: Nervous is the adjective and nervously the adverb: a nervous wait, but he waited nervously.
normal.cn: nervous 是形容词，nervously 是副词：说 a nervous wait，但说 he waited nervously。

normal.en: The ending -ly goes back to Old English -lice and means in the manner of, so nervously names the way, not the feeling.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 可追到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」，所以 nervously 命名的是方式，而不是感受。

normal.en: Nervously keeps the tight-thread picture of nerve, which is why it suits tapping feet and turning pens.
normal.cn: nervously 保留了 nerve 那根绷紧细线的画面，所以它很适合形容跺脚与转笔。

normal.en: Laughing nervously and smiling nervously both show tension leaking into the face when words fail.
normal.cn: laugh nervously 与 smile nervously 都表现话说不下去时，紧张从脸上漏出来。

normal.en: In writing, nervously often marks a character who is trying too hard to seem calm.

senses.definitionCN: 一成不变地重复、因而变得乏味的东西
senses.example: The film avoids the usual stereotype.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影避开了常见的固定套路。
senses.why: A printed plate always gives the same image.
senses.whyCN: 印版印出的永远是同一幅图。

senses.title: Printing plate
senses.definition: a metal plate used to print the same page again
senses.definitionCN: 用于重复印刷同一页面的金属版
senses.example: The printer kept the old stereotype.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷工保留着旧铅版。
senses.why: This is the original technical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最初的技术义项。

intro.en: Stereotype joins Greek stereos, solid, with type, a printed impression.
intro.cn: stereotype 由希腊语 stereos（坚固的）与 type（印刷的印痕）组合而成。

items.en: Stereos meant solid or firm.
items.cn: stereos 意为坚固的。

items.en: The printing term entered through French.
items.cn: 这个印刷术语经由法语传入。

items.en: A stereotype was a fixed printing plate.
items.cn: stereotype 指固定的印刷铅版。

items.en: The word came to mean a fixed idea.
items.cn: 这个词转而指固定的观念。

items.en: It now names unfair general ideas about groups.
items.cn: 现在它指对群体不公平的笼统看法。

note.en: Stereotype is compared with look-alike words and with words for fixed ideas.
note.cn: 把 stereotype 与形近词以及表示固定观念的词作比较。

entries.definition: a first model
a perfect original example
sound from two directions
an unfair opinion formed without knowledge
an overused phrase or idea
a simple name put on a group

normalIntro.en: A stereotype is one plate stamped again and again until every face looks the same.
normalIntro.cn: 刻板印象，就是一块版反复压印，直到每张脸看起来都一样。

normal.en: The film plays on an old stereotype.
normal.cn: 这部电影利用了一个老套的成见。

normal.en: Do not judge people by stereotype.
normal.cn: 不要用刻板印象评判人。

normal.en: Gender stereotypes still exist.
normal.cn: 性别刻板印象仍然存在。

normal.en: She does not fit the stereotype.
normal.cn: 她并不符合那个刻板形象。

normal.en: Education can break stereotypes.
normal.cn: 教育能打破成见。

abstract.en: A fixed image saves thinking and costs justice.
abstract.cn: 固定的形象省了思考，却赔上了公正。

abstract.en: A plate prints the same face on every page.
abstract.cn: 一块版，会在每一页印出同一张脸。

abstract.en: What repeats too easily stops seeing.
abstract.cn: 过于轻易重复的东西，就不再看得见。

examples.en: She broke the stereotype of nurses.
examples.cn: 她打破了人们对护士的刻板印象。

examples.en: The film avoids the usual stereotype.
examples.cn: 这部电影避开了常见的固定套路。

examples.en: Gender stereotypes still exist.
examples.cn: 性别刻板印象仍然存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: stereotype 原是印刷用的「铅版」，一块版反复印出同样的图，后来引申为人们脑中反复复制的「刻板印象」。

root: 希腊语 stereos（坚固的）加 type（印痕），本指固定铅版；因铅版反复印出同一图案，引申为固定不变的形象与成见。

sensesIntro.en: Stereotype is a fixed idea about a group, a dull repeated pattern, or the printing plate behind the image.
sensesIntro.cn: stereotype 是对某群体的固定看法、乏味的重复模式，或产生这种形象的印版。

core.en: One plate stamping the same picture.
core.cn: 一块版反复印出同一幅画。

branches.en: A whole group is described with one sentence.
branches.cn: 用一个句子描述一整群人。

branches.en: A story repeats the same scene again.
branches.cn: 一个故事又重复同一个场景。

branches.en: A metal plate waits on a press.
branches.cn: 一块金属版等在印刷机上。

branches.en: The printing plate is the image of a fixed mind.
branches.cn: 铅版，正是一颗僵化头脑的形象。

branches.en: What is printed the same way never surprises.
branches.cn: 以同样方式印出来的东西，从不出人意料。

intro.en: Stereotype builds adjectives with -ed and -ical, and a noun with -ing.
intro.cn: stereotype 加 -ed 与 -ical 构成形容词，加 -ing 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek: stereos, solid, and typos, a stamp.
latinIntro.cn: 其构件来自希腊语：stereos（坚固的）与 typos（印痕）。

items.exampleCN: 刻板化会伤害真实的人。
这是一种刻板化的看法。

definition_zh: 体贴的；考虑周到的；沉思的；有思想的
definition_en: showing care for other people’s needs, or given to quiet and serious thinking
core_image: 一个人先在心里替你走一遍路，再把伞递到你手上
scene: 下雨的清晨，室友没说话，只在门口多放了一把伞和一张便条。 It was thoughtful of her to leave an umbrella by the door on such a wet morning.
sceneCN: 这里 thoughtful 是「体贴的、考虑周到的」（第 1 个义项：替他人着想并付诸行动）；句意为她在这样的雨天把伞放在门口，真是体贴。

derivatives.zh: 由 think 不规则变化而来的名词，义为「想法；思考」，是 thoughtful 的词基
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「体贴地；沉思地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「体贴；周到；深思」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不体贴的；考虑不周的」

senses.title: Considerate of other people
senses.definition: showing that you think about other people’s feelings and needs and act to help
senses.definitionCN: 表现出替他人的感受与需要着想，并付诸行动
senses.example: It was thoughtful of him to call before dropping by.
senses.exampleCN: 他来访前先打了个电话，真是体贴。
senses.why: Thought plus the suffix -ful turns the inner act of thinking outward, into care for someone else.
senses.whyCN: thought 加上后缀 -ful，把内心的思考转向外部，变成对他人的照顾。

senses.title: Showing careful thought
senses.definition: carefully planned or considered, so that nothing important is forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细计划或考虑，重要之处都没有遗漏
senses.example: The report offers a thoughtful analysis of the housing problem.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对住房问题做了考虑周到的分析。
senses.why: The same fullness of thought is applied to a piece of work rather than to a person.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「思虑充盈」被用到一件作品上，而不是一个人身上。

senses.title: Quietly absorbed in thought
senses.definition: looking serious and quiet because you are thinking about something
senses.definitionCN: 因在思考某事而显得严肃、安静
senses.example: She sat by the window with a thoughtful expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，一副若有所思的神情。
senses.why: This is the literal picture: a person whose face shows that the mind is full of thought.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的画面：脸上显出内心塞满思绪的人。

senses.title: Having serious ideas
senses.definition: showing serious and original ideas, of a person, book or film
senses.definitionCN: 指人、书或影片呈现出严肃而有独到见解的思想
senses.example: He is a thoughtful writer who asks uncomfortable questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位有思想的作家，总提让人不适的问题。
senses.why: A mind that is always full of thought is valued for the quality of what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 总是装满意绪的心灵，因其所装之物的分量而受到重视。

intro.en: Thoughtful is a native English compound: the noun thought plus the full-suffix -ful.
intro.cn: thoughtful 是英语本土复合词：名词 thought 加表示「充满」的后缀 -ful。

items.en: The root behind think meant to seem or to appear to the mind, a sense still visible in an old legal phrase.
items.cn: think 背后的词根意为「在心中显现」，这一含义还残留在古老的固定说法里。

items.en: Old English had the verb for thinking and the noun for a thought, built on an old nominal form.
items.cn: 古英语已有表示「思考」的动词与表示「想法」的名词，建立在古老的名词形式上。

items.en: The adjective formed with -ful of thought appears in the Middle English period, first in the sense of being deep in thought.
items.cn: 由 thought 加 -ful 构成的形容词出现于中古英语时期，最初义为「陷入深思的」。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word had moved outward: thoughtful came to mean considerate of other people.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词向外转：thoughtful 开始表示「替他人着想的」。

items.en: Modern use keeps both directions side by side, the inner thinker and the outward kindness.
items.cn: 现代用法让两个方向并存：内心的思考者与向外的善意。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on thought; the second compares words of consideration and thinking.
note.cn: 第一组收以 thought 为词基的一族词；第二组比较表示体贴与思考的词。

entries.definition: The noun for an idea or the act of thinking, also the past of think.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想法；思考」，也是 think 的过去式

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a considerate or meditative way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「体贴地；沉思地」

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being considerate or deep in thought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「体贴、周到、深思」

entries.definition: Grateful; it rhymes with thoughtful and uses the same suffix but another base, so the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 感激的；与本词押韵且后缀相同，但词基不同，词源不同

entries.definition: Careful not to trouble or hurt others; the closest formal partner of thoughtful.
entries.definitionCN: 体贴的；为他人着想的（最接近的正式近义词）

entries.definition: Paying close attention to someone and their needs.
entries.definitionCN: 殷勤的；关注他人需要的

entries.definition: Showing love and concern for others, warmer and more emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 关心人的（更温暖、更多情感色彩）

entries.definition: Quietly thinking, often with a hint of sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思的（带一丝忧愁，文学色彩）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the base noun, the suffix -ful, and the outward turn the word took.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自词基名词、后缀 -ful，以及这个词后来向外的转向。

normal.en: Thoughtful is thought plus -ful: a head full of thought, aimed at someone else.
normal.cn: thoughtful 就是 thought 加 -ful：满脑子思绪，只是朝着别人的方向。

normal.en: A thoughtful gift shows that someone thought about you before choosing it.
normal.cn: 贴心的礼物说明有人先想到你，才去挑选。

normal.en: A thoughtful silence is a thinking silence, not an angry one.
normal.cn: thoughtful silence 是思考的静默，不是生气的静默。

normal.en: The adverb is thoughtfully, the noun thoughtfulness.
normal.cn: 副词是 thoughtfully，名词是 thoughtfulness。

normal.en: Do not mix it with thankful: one is care, the other is gratitude.
normal.cn: 不要与 thankful 相混：一个是体贴，一个是感激。

abstract.en: Picture someone walking your day in their head before it happens, then leaving what you will need.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在心里先把你的一天走一遍，然后把你需要的东西留下。

abstract.en: Thought is water; the suffix -ful makes it a cup filled to the brim, offered to someone.
abstract.cn: 思绪是水，后缀 -ful 让它成为满满一杯，端给别人。

abstract.en: The word points both inward to the quiet thinker and outward to the quiet helper.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指向内心的默想者，也指向安静的帮忙者。

examples.en: It was thoughtful of you to remember my birthday.
examples.cn: 你还记得我的生日，真是体贴。

examples.en: She gave the plan a thoughtful review before agreeing.
examples.cn: 她在同意前对这个计划做了周密的审视。

examples.en: He grew thoughtful whenever the name was mentioned.
examples.cn: 一提到那个名字，他就陷入沉思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「梭特福」——心里来回穿梭,把福气先留给别人 → thoughtful 体贴的

root: 英语本土复合：thought（think 的不规则名词形，源自古英语表示「思考」的词）+ 后缀 -ful「充满……的」；最初指「陷入深思」，十八世纪起扩展为「替他人着想的」。

sensesIntro.en: Thoughtful fills the head with thought and then points it in two directions: outward to other people and their needs, inward to a quiet thinking mind.
sensesIntro.cn: thoughtful 让头脑装满思绪，再把这份思绪指向两个方向：向外给他人的需要，向内给安静的思考者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walking someone else’s day inside your head, then leaving what they will need.
core.cn: 核心意象：在心里先替别人走一遍他的一天，再留下他会需要的东西。

branches.en: The person: thought turned into kindness for others.
branches.cn: 人线：思绪转化为对他人的善意。

branches.en: The work: the same fullness of thought spent on a report or a plan.
branches.cn: 作品线：同样的思虑充沛被用在报告或计划上。

branches.en: The face: the literal picture of a mind at work.
branches.cn: 面容线：心灵运转时最字面的画面。

branches.en: The writer: thoughts valuable enough to be a reputation.
branches.cn: 作者线：思绪深到足以成为一种名声。

branches.en: Inner and outer halves of the same suffixed word.
branches.cn: 同一个带后缀词的向内与向外两半。

intro.en: Thoughtful is built natively with the suffix -ful, and English adds -ly and -ness on top.
intro.cn: thoughtful 由本土后缀 -ful 构成，英语再在其上叠加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: The base and suffix are both English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属英语，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: an idea; the act of thinking

items.example: We are thankful for your help.
A considerate host checks the heating.
items.exampleCN: 体贴的主人会查看暖气。

definition_zh: 真诚地；由衷地
definition_en: in an honest and true way
core_image: 写信人在信末郑重写下自己的名字
scene: 我真诚地希望你能原谅我。 I sincerely hope you can forgive me.
sceneCN: 这里 sincerely 是「真诚地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我真诚地希望你能原谅我。

derivatives.zh: 真诚的
真诚

senses.title: In an honest way
senses.definition: with real feeling and no pretense
senses.definitionCN: 带着真实情感而不装假
senses.example: I sincerely hope you can forgive me.
senses.exampleCN: 我真诚地希望你能原谅我。
senses.why: This is the adverb form of sincere.
senses.whyCN: 这是 sincere 的副词形式。

senses.title: As a letter closing
senses.definition: used before a name to close a formal letter
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式书信署名之前的结束语
senses.example: Yours sincerely, Li Ming.
senses.exampleCN: 您真诚的，李明。
senses.why: The closing repeats the promise of honest feeling.
senses.whyCN: 书信结尾再次表明真诚之情。

intro.en: Sincerely is sincere with the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: sincerely 是 sincere 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Sincerus meant pure or clean.
items.cn: sincerus 意为纯净或洁净。

items.en: Sincere carried the sense of purity.
items.cn: sincere 带有纯粹的含义。

items.en: Sincere entered English as an adjective.
items.cn: sincere 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb sincerely grew from it.
items.cn: 副词 sincerely 由它派生。

items.en: It became a standard letter closing.
items.cn: 它成为标准的书信结束语。

note.en: Sincerely is compared with similar-looking words and words for honesty.
note.cn: 把 sincerely 与形近词以及表示诚实的词作比较。

entries.definition: almost not
safely
honesty of feeling
truthfully
really
seriously and warmly

normalIntro.en: Sincerely marks words that come from the heart.
normalIntro.cn: sincerely 标记发自内心的话。

normal.en: I sincerely hope you can forgive me.
normal.cn: 我真诚地希望你能原谅我。

normal.en: She sincerely apologized for the delay.
normal.cn: 她为延误真诚地道歉。

normal.en: I sincerely believe your plan will work.
normal.cn: 我由衷地相信你的计划会成功。

normal.en: Yours sincerely, Li Ming.
normal.cn: 您真诚的，李明。

normal.en: He sincerely thanked every helper.
normal.cn: 他衷心感谢每一位帮手。

abstract.en: A sincere word is a hand held out.
abstract.cn: 真诚的话是一只伸出的手。

abstract.en: Thanks said sincerely weigh more than gifts.
abstract.cn: 真诚说出的感谢比礼物更重。

abstract.en: The heart signs every sincere letter.
abstract.cn: 每一封真诚的信都由心来署名。

examples.en: I sincerely hope you can forgive me.
examples.cn: 我真诚地希望你能原谅我。

examples.en: She sincerely apologized for the delay.
examples.cn: 她为延误真诚地道歉。

examples.en: Yours sincerely, Li Ming.
examples.cn: 您真诚的，李明。

dict_mnemonic.text: sincere（真诚的）+ -ly（副词后缀）= sincerely；信件结尾 Yours sincerely 相当于中文的「谨启、您真诚的」。

root: 由拉丁语 sincerus（纯净的）经古法语 sincere 进入英语，再加副词后缀 -ly。

sensesIntro.en: Sincerely means in an honest way or as a formal letter closing.
sensesIntro.cn: sincerely 意为真诚地，或用作书信结束语。

core.en: Words that carry the heart without a mask.
core.cn: 不加面具、承载真心的话。

branches.en: A hope is spoken without pretending.
branches.cn: 希望被说出，没有伪装。

branches.en: A name follows the closing line.
branches.cn: 署名跟在结束语之后。

branches.en: The letter closing repeats the same honesty.
branches.cn: 书信结尾重复着同样的诚实。

branches.en: An apology is offered with a clear face.
branches.cn: 道歉时神情坦然。

branches.en: Every formal letter ends with a promise of truth.
branches.cn: 每封正式书信都以真诚的承诺结尾。

intro.en: Sincerely shows -ly turning honest feeling into an adverb.
intro.cn: sincerely 展示了 -ly 把真诚情感变成副词。

latinIntro.en: Sincerely goes back to Latin sincerus.
latinIntro.cn: sincerely 可追溯至拉丁语 sincerus。

items.exampleCN: 我们真诚地希望你康复。

items.example: I sincerely believe she is right.
items.exampleCN: 我由衷地相信她是对的。

definition_zh: 英亩；田地；地产
definition_en: a unit of land area, or a piece of land measured in such units
core_image: 一头牛拉着犁，一天走完的那片方方正正的田
scene: 这个家庭农场占地约四十英亩。 The family farm covers about forty acres.
sceneCN: 这里的 acre 是「英亩」（第 1 个义项：土地面积单位）；句意是这个家庭农场约有四十英亩。

derivatives.zh: 由 acre 加集合名词后缀构成，义为「英亩数；土地面积」
由 acre 加形容词词尾构成，义为「拥有田地的」（多见于旧文学）

senses.title: A unit of land area
senses.definition: a measure of land equal to about four thousand square metres
senses.definitionCN: 一种土地面积单位，约合四千平方米
senses.example: They keep two horses on five acres.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在五英亩地上养了两匹马。
senses.why: The Old English word named a field itself, and the measure grew out of how much land a team could plough in a day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本指一块田，而面积单位是从「一队牛一天能犁多少地」长出来的。

senses.title: Land or grounds
senses.definition: a stretch of land, often used in the plural for an estate
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地，常用复数指一整处地产
senses.example: The old house stands in acres of green lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子坐落在成片绿草坪中。
senses.why: Because the word first meant a field, the plural can still mean land as property rather than a number on a survey.
senses.whyCN: 因为这词最初就指一块田，所以复数至今仍可指作为产业的土地，而不是图纸上的一个数字。

intro.en: The word is an old Germanic field term, related to Latin ager.
intro.cn: 这是一个古老的日耳曼语田地词，与拉丁语 ager 同源。

items.en: a reconstructed root meant field or pasture.
items.cn: 一个重构词根意为田地或牧场。

items.en: the root became a word for an open field.
items.cn: 这个词根变成表示开阔田地的词。

items.en: æcer meant a field, especially a ploughed one.
items.cn: æcer 意为田地，尤指犁过的田。

items.en: the word also became a fixed measure of land.
items.cn: 这个词同时也成了固定的土地面积单位。

items.en: acre now measures plots from gardens to farms.
items.cn: 如今 acre 丈量从园子到农场的各类地块。

note.en: The first group shares the acre stem; the second is other land measures and land words.
note.cn: 第一组共享 acre 词干；第二组是别的土地计量与土地词。

entries.definition: an area of land measured in acres
owning land
plots of land in the plural
the Latin word for a field
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示田地的词

entries.definition: a metric unit of land area
an open piece of farmland
a small measured piece of land
a large area of land owned by one person

normalIntro.en: The word is cousin to Latin ager, field, and to agriculture.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与拉丁语 ager（田地）以及 agriculture 是亲戚。

normal.en: æcer meant a ploughed field before it meant a measure.
normal.cn: æcer 先指犁过的田，后来才指面积单位。

normal.en: an acre is roughly the land a team could plough in a day.
normal.cn: 一英亩大致是一队牛一天能犁完的地。

normal.en: acreage is the collective noun for the size of a farm.
normal.cn: acreage 是表示农场面积的集合名词。

normal.en: per acre is the phrase used for crop yields.
normal.cn: per acre 是计算亩产的固定说法。

normal.en: the plural acres often suggests a large estate.
normal.cn: 复数 acres 常暗示一大片地产。

abstract.en: See an ox team turning at the end of a square field.
abstract.cn: 想象一队牛在方形田的尽头转弯。

abstract.en: Picture a farmhouse surrounded by a green sea of lawn.
abstract.cn: 想象农舍四周是一片绿色的草坪海。

abstract.en: Think of a deed with the land size written in acres.
abstract.cn: 想象一份地契，面积一栏写着英亩数。

examples.en: The vineyard covers thirty acres of hillside.
examples.cn: 这片葡萄园占了三十英亩山坡。

examples.en: They bought an acre of woodland behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们买下了屋后一英亩林地。

examples.en: The farmer counts every acre before planting.
examples.cn: 农民播种前把每一英亩都算清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶克」——老农用手一「诶」，圈出一大块方方正正的田。

root: 古英语 æcer（田地），源自原始日耳曼语，更早可追到印欧词根，与拉丁语 ager（田地）、agriculture 同源；本义是犁过的田，后成为土地面积单位。

sensesIntro.en: A field word became a number, and the number still remembers the field.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「田」字变成了数字，而这个数字仍记得那片田。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square field marked out by a plough.
core.cn: 核心意象：被犁沟圈出的方形田。

branches.en: a number used to price or sell land
branches.cn: 用来给土地定价或出售的数字

branches.en: grounds rolling away from an old house
branches.cn: 从老屋向外铺开的园地

branches.en: yields quoted per acre
branches.cn: 按英亩计算的产量

branches.en: an estate measured in broad acres
branches.cn: 以大片英亩计的地产

branches.en: land at once counted and owned
branches.cn: 既被计数又被拥有的土地

intro.en: The word is a Germanic field term; its endings are English, not Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语的田地词，词尾是英语的，不是拉丁的。

latinIntro.en: Its distant Latin cousin is ager, field, which gives agriculture and agrarian.
latinIntro.cn: 它在拉丁语里的远亲是 ager（田地），后者给出 agriculture 与 agrarian。

definition_zh: 麦克风；传声器；话筒；窃听器
definition_en: a device that picks up sound and turns it into an electrical signal, especially the part a performer speaks into or a small hidden pickup
core_image: 一根细长的杆，把说话声收进一道看不见的电信号
scene: 演播室里，主持人把支架拉近，确认声音能送到最后一排观众的耳朵。 The host leaned toward the microphone and opened the show.
sceneCN: 这里是「话筒」（第 2 个义项：供人对着说话的部件）；句意为主持人俯身靠近话筒开始节目。图中可辨识物件：话筒架、演播台、指示灯。

pos.zh: 麦克风；传声器；话筒；窃听器

derivatives.zh: 由 microphone 缩略而来，口语中读作单音节，义为「麦克风」
由 microphone 加 -ic 构成，义为「微音效应的；拾音引起的」
由 microphone 加 -y 构成，义为「微音效应」

senses.title: A device that turns sound into a signal
senses.definition: an instrument that picks up sound waves and converts them into an electrical signal
senses.definitionCN: 拾取声波并把它转换成电信号的器件
senses.example: A microphone on the table picked up every word of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的传声器把会议的每句话都收了进去。
senses.why: The Greek pieces say small sound, and early devices were built to make faint sounds audible, so the name describes catching sound rather than producing it.
senses.whyCN: 两个希腊词素说的是「微小的声音」，早期装置正是为了让微弱的声音能被听见，所以名字描述的是捕捉声音，而非发出声音。

senses.title: The part a performer speaks into
senses.definition: the part of a sound system, headset or instrument that a person speaks or sings directly into
senses.definitionCN: 音响、耳机或乐器上供人直接对着说话或演唱的部件
senses.example: She held the microphone close and lowered her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她把话筒拿近，压低声音唱。
senses.why: Once the signal device is placed in front of a performer, the word stops naming the circuit and starts naming the object aimed at the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 当这种转换器件被摆到表演者嘴前，词义就不再指电路，而开始指那个对准嘴巴的物件。

senses.title: A hidden listening device
senses.definition: a small hidden device that picks up speech so that someone can listen without being seen
senses.definitionCN: 暗藏的小型拾音装置，使人在不被看见的情况下听到谈话
senses.example: They found a microphone under the desk in the empty office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在空办公室的书桌下面发现了一个窃听器。
senses.why: A device built to catch tiny sounds is exactly what surveillance needs, so the technical name quietly took on the meaning of a bug hidden in a room.
senses.whyCN: 能捕捉细微声响的器件正是监听所需，于是这个技术名称自然而然地多了「藏在房间里的窃听器」这层意思。

intro.en: Microphone is a nineteenth-century coinage from two Greek words, small and voice, and its use moved from faint-sound devices to the electric pickup everyone knows.
intro.cn: microphone 是十九世纪用两个希腊词「小」与「声音」拼成的新词，用法从放大微弱声音的装置转到了人人熟悉的电声拾音器。

items.en: Mikros meant small or little, and it became the first element of many scientific words.
items.cn: mikros 意为小的、细微的，后来成为许多科学词汇的第一个词素。

items.en: Phone meant voice or sound, and it named both the human voice and the sound itself.
items.cn: phone 意为嗓音或声音，既指人的说话声，也指声音本身。

items.en: Writers of scientific Latin and English joined the two elements to name devices for making weak sounds easier to hear; the exact first coining is not settled.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语与英语的作者把两个词素拼起来，命名让微弱声音更容易被听见的装置；具体首见年份尚无定论。

items.en: With carbon transmitters and early telephony, the word settled on the device that converts sound into an electric current.
items.cn: 随着碳粒送话器和早期电话技术，这个词固定指把声音转换成电流的器件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the technical sense and extends it to the pickup on a headset and to a hidden listening bug.
items.cn: 现代英语保留技术义，并把它扩展到耳机上的拾音件和暗藏的窃听装置。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek voice element through short forms and compounds; the near-meaning group collects the other pieces of a sound chain.
note.cn: 形近组顺着希腊语「声音」词素，收简称与复合词；近义组收一条声音链路里的其他器件。

entries.definition: The short spoken form of microphone.
A device for speaking to someone at a distance; it shares the voice element.
entries.definitionCN: 远距离通话的装置，与 microphone 共用表示「声音」的词素。

entries.definition: A cone that makes a voice carry much farther.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音传得更远的锥形扩音器。

entries.definition: One of the distinct speech sounds of a language.
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言中彼此区别的语音单位。

entries.definition: A device that turns an electric signal back into sound.
entries.definitionCN: 把电信号还原成声音的装置。

entries.definition: A device that makes a signal stronger before it is sent on.
entries.definitionCN: 在信号送出前把它增强的装置。

entries.definition: A pair of earpieces with a pickup, worn on the head.
entries.definitionCN: 带拾音件的头戴式耳机。

entries.definition: The small part of a device that sits close to the ear.
entries.definitionCN: 设备上贴近耳朵的小部件。

normalIntro.en: Two Greek pieces, small and voice, were joined in the nineteenth century to name a device that catches sound.
normalIntro.cn: 两个希腊词素「小」与「声音」在十九世纪拼在一起，用来命名一种捕捉声音的器件。

normal.en: Micro- means small and -phone means voice, so the compound says small voice before it says anything technical.
normal.cn: micro- 意为「小」，-phone 意为「声音」，所以这个复合词先说的是「小声音」，然后才谈技术。

normal.en: Telephone and megaphone share the same voice element, one for distance and one for reach of volume.
normal.cn: telephone 与 megaphone 共用同一个「声音」词素，一个指距离，一个指音量传得远。

normal.en: Phoneme, phonetics and symphony all descend from the Greek word for voice.
normal.cn: phoneme、phonetics 与 symphony 都出自希腊语中表示「声音」的词。

normal.en: Audio workers write mic, not mike, for the short form, and the spelling marks the trade.
normal.cn: 音频行业把简称写作 mic 而不是 mike，这个拼写本身就是行内标记。

normal.en: A microphone converts rather than creates: the sound must exist before the device can turn it into a signal.
normal.cn: 麦克风只是转换，并不创造：声音必须先存在，器件才能把它变成信号。

abstract.en: A small voice made wide enough to fill a hall.
abstract.cn: 一个很小的声音被放大到能填满整个大厅。

abstract.en: The same pickup can serve a singer and a spy; the tool leaves the purpose to the hand that places it.
abstract.cn: 同一个拾音器可以服务歌手，也可以服务间谍；工具把用途留给摆放它的那只手。

abstract.en: Sound has no shape, yet a microphone gives it something a wire can carry.
abstract.cn: 声音本没有形状，麦克风却给了它一样能被导线带走的东西。

examples.en: She checked the microphone before the interview.
examples.cn: 采访前她检查了话筒。

examples.en: The microphone hidden in the lamp had been there for weeks.
examples.cn: 藏在台灯里的窃听器已经在那里放了好几周。

examples.en: The microphone on the stand was too far from the singer.
examples.cn: 支架上的话筒离歌手太远了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克风」——中文直接音译，麦克风就是 microphone 的常用叫法。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）与 phone（声音）拼接而成，十九世纪出现，指把声音拾取并转换为电信号的器件；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the conversion of sound into a signal; the senses divide into the pickup, the object a performer faces, and the same device used in secret.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把声音变成信号；义项分到拾音器件、表演者面对的那件物品，以及同一类器件的暗中用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin rod standing in front of a speaker, catching every word into an invisible wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细杆立在说话人面前，把每句话收进一根看不见的线。

branches.en: a faint voice made visible on a screen
branches.cn: 微弱的声音在屏幕上显成一道波形

branches.en: a singer leaning into a stand
branches.cn: 歌手俯身靠近支架

branches.en: a tiny device under a desk
branches.cn: 书桌底下的小装置

branches.en: sound caught first as a signal and then as a performance
branches.cn: 声音先被当作信号收下，再被当作表演送出

branches.en: the same pickup used openly and in secret
branches.cn: 同一个拾音器，一明一暗地用着

intro.en: A Greek prefix for small and a Greek combining form for voice sit on either side of the word, and later English shortenings and compounds extend the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「小」的希腊前缀与一个表示「声音」的希腊构词成分夹住这个词，后来的英语简称与复合词又把词族向外延伸。

latinIntro.en: The word was assembled from Greek elements in the nineteenth century, so no classical Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪用希腊词素拼出来的，古典拉丁语中没有它的同族词记录。
